reason: Pre-existing divergence surfaced by the leading-underscore call candidate (RFC 0106): the widened candidate list opens the ported-with-args gate on this call, which previously withheld the row. has_many_association.rb:91 `target.select!(&:new_record?)` mutates the target array in place; the port hands the retained subset to `_writeTargetStore`, the only sanctioned way to replace the target store.
Ruby `options.fetch(:ensuring_owner_was, nil)` (has_many_association.rb:52); a JS object has no `fetch`, so the stored-nil semantics are spelled as an own-key check at the call site.
Ruby `target.first.class` (has_many_association.rb:36); JS arrays have no `first`, so the same element is read as `this.target[0]`.
